transcript: Doctor: Good morning, what brings you in today? Patient: I've been having this really bad chest pain since last night. It's like a pressure in the center of my chest and it goes down my left arm. Doctor: When did it start exactly? Patient: Around 2 AM, I woke up with it. It's been constant. I also feel nauseous and short of breath. Doctor: Have you had any similar episodes before? Patient: No, never this bad. I do have high blood pressure and high cholesterol. I take lisinopril 10 milligrams and atorvastatin 40 milligrams. Doctor: Okay. Let me examine you. Blood pressure is 165 over 95, heart rate 102, respiratory rate 22, oxygen saturation 94 percent on room air. Temperature 37.1. On auscultation, I hear an S4 gallop. No murmurs. Lungs are clear bilaterally. ECG shows ST elevation in leads V1 through V4. Troponin is 2.8, elevated. Assessment: Acute anterior STEMI. Plan: Start aspirin 325 milligrams stat, heparin drip per protocol, nitroglycerin sublingual, morphine 4 milligrams IV for pain. Activate cath lab immediately. Continue home medications. NPO for potential PCI.

DIALOGUE:
Doctor: Good morning, what brings you in today?
Patient: Really bad chest pain since last night, pressure in center of chest radiating to left arm.
Doctor: When did it start exactly?
Patient: Around 2 AM, constant. Also nauseous and short of breath.
Doctor: Have you had similar episodes?
Patient: No. Has high blood pressure and high cholesterol. Takes lisinopril 10mg and atorvastatin 40mg.

SUBJECTIVE:
Patient presents with acute onset chest pain since 2 AM, described as central pressure radiating to left arm. Associated nausea and dyspnea. No prior similar episodes. PMH: hypertension, hyperlipidemia. Current medications: lisinopril 10mg, atorvastatin 40mg.

OBJECTIVE:
Vitals: BP 165/95, HR 102, RR 22, SpO2 94% RA, Temp 37.1°C
Cardiac: S4 gallop present, no murmurs
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
ECG: ST elevation V1-V4
Labs: Troponin 2.8 (elevated)

ASSESSMENT:
Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)

PLAN:
1. Aspirin 325mg stat
2. Heparin drip per protocol
3. Nitroglycerin sublingual
4. Morphine 4mg IV for pain
5. Activate cath lab for emergent PCI
6. Continue home medications
7. NPO status
